chunks: And this hadith was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Babawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: The people narrate that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted the month of Ramadan twenty-nine days more often than he fasted thirty days. He said: They lied. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not fast except complete, and the obligations are not deficient. Indeed, Allah created the year as three hundred and sixty days, and He created the heavens and the earth in six days, so He withheld them from the three hundred and sixty days; thus the year is three hundred and fifty-four days, and the month of Ramadan is thirty days. And he continued the hadith to its end.

key_terms.السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ: the heavens and the earth, mentioned in relation to creation in six days
key_terms.السَّنَةَ: the year, discussed in terms of its created measure
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضُ: the obligatory religious duties, described here as not being deficient
key_terms.ثَلَاثُونَ يَوْمًا: thirty days, stated here as the full measure of Ramadan
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم mentioned as the exemplar in fasting Ramadan
key_terms.شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the obligatory month of fasting

ai.seo_question: Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fast Ramadan as twenty-nine days more often than thirty?
ai.summary: This hadith reports Imam Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام rejecting the claim that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم usually fasted Ramadan as twenty-nine days. It presents Ramadan as a complete thirty-day obligation and links the reckoning of the lunar year to the creation of the heavens and the earth in six days.
